about: Hunahpu and Xbalanque go off happily to play ball on the court of their fathers, far from home, and sweep it clean. The lords of Xibalba hear them overhead: who are these playing again over their heads? Did not Hunhunahpu and Vucub Hunahpu die? Huncame and Vucub Came send their messengers: the boys are to come and play in seven days. The messengers come straight down the road to the house, find the grandmother eating, and give her the day. When they have gone her heart breaks: so, long ago, the messengers came for the boys' fathers. A louse drops from her; she picks it up and sends it with the message. On the road a toad, Tamazul, offers to carry the slow louse and swallows it; a great snake, Zaquicaz, swallows the toad, and the falcon swallows the snake. That, the text says, is why snakes eat toads and hawks eat snakes. The falcon lights on the wall of the ball court crying “vacco”; the twins shoot it in the eye with a blowgun, heal the eye with a little of the ball's rubber, and the falcon brings up the snake, which brings up the toad. The toad cannot bring up the louse; the boys kick it, open its mouth, and find the louse stuck in its gums, never swallowed at all. The louse gives the message: in seven days, with their ball gear, at Xibalba; your grandmother is weeping. The twins go home to take their leave. Each will plant a cane in the middle of the house: if the canes dry up, they are dead; if they put out shoots, they are alive. “Do not weep,” they tell their grandmother and their mother; and they plant the canes in dry earth in the middle of the house.

sentences.t: Que quicot chicut xe bec echaahel, pa hom; naht cu xe chaahic qui tuquel; xqui mez ri hom qui cahau.
sentences.l: They rejoice again-then they-went players(?), at ball-court; far then they-played their-alone; they-swept the ball-court their-father(s).
sentences.i: And so, rejoicing, they went off once more to play, to the ball court; far off they played, on their own, and they swept the ball court of their fathers.
sentences.n: Ximénez indents a paragraph here; Brasseur begins his seventh chapter. Que quicot 'they rejoice': que, k- 'ongoing' + e 'they', + quicot 'be glad' (001). chicut 'again then', chic + cut written as one word. xe bec 'they went': x- + e 'they' + bec (b'ek, as earlier parts). echaahel is written as one word; Brasseur divides e chaahel, e 'they (are)' + chaah 'play (ball)' + agent -el, 'as players' (inferred; the agent noun is not met before). hom 'the ball court' (009). naht 'far' (najt): Brasseur 'bien loin'. xe chaahic 'they played': the MS looks like chauhic, and Brasseur's chaahic is taken. qui tuquel 'on their own', as vtuquel 'alone' with qui- 'their'. xqui mez 'they swept': mez 'sweep', as in the mezcutahinac of the last part (Brasseur 'balayer'). qui cahau 'their father(s)': Hunhunahpu and Vucub Hunahpu, who played on this court before they were summoned.

sentences.t: Ta xquita cu vloc rahaual Xibalba: “Apa china chiri mi xu tiquiba chic etzanem pa ca vi? Ma pa que quixbic que nicnot vloc?
sentences.l: Then they-heard then hither the-lords Xibalba: “Where(?) who there just-now he-began again playing at our head? Not (pa) they fear(?) they shake(?) hither?
sentences.i: Then the lords of Xibalba heard them: “Who are these, then, who have just begun again to play over our heads? Have they no fear (?), shaking things (?) up there?
sentences.n: The manuscript has mi xuhquiba, a misprint for mi xu tiquiba, corrected here: the t is the h-like t of this hand, and the i is missing (Brasseur tiqiba). xquita 'they heard': x- + qui- 'they' + ta 'hear'. rahaual Xibalba 'the lords of Xibalba': r- 'its' + ahau 'lord' + -al. Apa china 'who (are they)': apa is 'where' elsewhere, china 'who' (Brasseur 'Qui donc sont ceux…'); the pair is read as one question (inferred). mi xu tiquiba 'he has just begun': mi 'just now', x- + v- (singular, as in the fixed xrah construction) + tiquiba 'begin' (the planting verb, as at the opening of the last part). etzanem 'playing', an -em noun of etz' 'play'; it is written with plain t + z, not the ligature, and the toggle gives the modern word, etz'anem, as the published queꜩabal (ketz'ab'al, 009, 010, 016) and the quetzabal of ¶17 (006's eꜩeyah was left etzeyaj; the two should be brought together). pa ca vi 'over our heads': vi 'head, top' (wi', as 013's juwi'). quixbic and nicnot are not known: Brasseur has 'qui ne craignent point d'ébranler (la terre)', and the English follows him, marked (?); both are respelled by the letters.

sentences.t: Ma pa xe cam ri Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu, xrah qui nimarizah quib chi ca vach? He cu itaca chic,” xeꜭha chic ri Hun Came, Vvcub Came, conohel ahauab.
sentences.l: Not (pa) they-died the Hunhunahpu, Vvcub Hunahpu, it-wanted their making-great themselves before our face? Go(?) then you-summon again,” they-said again the Hun Came, Vvcub Came, all lords.
sentences.i: Did they not die, Hunhunahpu and Vucub Hunahpu, who wanted to make themselves great before our faces? Go, then, and summon these in their turn,” said Huncame and Vucub Came and all the lords.
sentences.n: Ma pa 'did not … ?', a question expecting yes. xe cam 'they died' (kam 'die'). Hunhunahpu and Vvcub Hunahpu are the twins' father and uncle, who died in Xibalba (009–012); here Hunhunahpu is the right name. xrah qui nimarizah quib 'they wanted to exalt themselves': the singular xrah with the plural qui-, the fixed construction of earlier parts; nimarizah 'make great' (nima 'great' + -iza), quib 'themselves'. chi ca vach 'before our face'. He cu itaca chic: an ink blot covers the letter after he, and Brasseur reads He cu y taka; itaca is i- 'you (pl.)' + taca 'send for, summon' (as published), and he is taken, as in 010, as a form of 'go' (inferred): Brasseur 'Allez donc chercher ceux-ci à leur tour'. Hun Came is written here as two words; the English keeps the published Huncame. conohel ahauab 'all the lords'.

sentences.t: Xe taco vloc; xeꜭha cut chire qui zamahel: “Quixꜭha, quix oponic: Que petoc, queꜭha ahauab;
sentences.l: They-sent(?) hither; they-said then to-them their messenger(s): “You-shall-say, you-shall-arrive: Let-them come, say lords;
sentences.i: They sent word; they said to their messengers: “Go and say it when you arrive there: ‘Let them come,’ say the lords;
sentences.n: Xe taco vloc 'they sent (them) hither': taco is taq 'send, send for' + -o, the transitive ending; xe is the absolutive 'they', and no ergative is written: read with Brasseur ('Ils envoyèrent'), the lords are the senders and their qui- is unwritten; read as written, xe is the one sent, 'they (the messengers) were sent' or 'they (the boys) were sent for' (inferred either way). zamahel 'messenger': zamah 'errand' + agent -el (009). Quixꜭha 'you shall say': k- + ix 'you (pl.)' + ꜭha 'say'; quix oponic 'you shall arrive there'. The lords' own words follow inside the messengers' message: Que petoc 'let them come', que 'they' + pet 'come' + -oc. queꜭha 'they say', of the lords. The nested speech is printed inside one pair of quotation marks in the text; the English marks the inner level with single quotes.

sentences.t: varal tah coh chaah vi cuꜭ; vvcubix coh etzanic, quecha ahauab; quixꜭha quix oponic,” xevꜭhax cut ri zamahel.
sentences.l: here (tah) we play (vi) with-them; in-seven-days we play, say lords; you-shall-say, you-shall-arrive,” were-told then the messenger(s).
sentences.i: ‘here we will play with them; in seven days we will play,’ say the lords. Go and say it when you arrive,” the messengers were told.
sentences.n: varal tah coh chaah vi cuꜭ 'here we shall play with them': coh, k- + oh 'we'; chaah 'play (ball)' (009); cuꜭ 'with them', the ruꜭ 'with him' of earlier parts with the 3pl prefix. vvcubix 'in seven days': vvcub 'seven' + -ix, the count of days ahead (Brasseur 'dans sept jours'). etzanic 'playing', the verb of etzanem in the last unit (mt etz'anik, as there). quecha 'they say' is written with plain ch, where the formula is usually ꜭh; printed as written (the toggle has kecha, the letters, as the published cacha). The order is said twice, quixꜭha quix oponic, at the start and end. xevꜭhax 'they were told': x- + e 'they' + vꜭhax, the published passive vꜭhax (uch'ax) with the v analysed as u-.

sentences.t: Ta xe pe cut, nima hoc cu qui be ri ꜭaholab chi cochoch, ca tocol chi cochoch;
sentences.l: Then they-came then, great cleared(?) then their road the boys at their-house, going-straight(?) at their-house;
sentences.i: So they came; and great was the road the boys had cleared (?) from their house, running straight (?) to their house;
sentences.n: xe pe 'they came', the messengers. nima hoc cu qui be ri ꜭaholab 'great hoc their road, the boys'': hoc is not otherwise known, and its sense is unclear; Brasseur prints nima 'hoc and translates 'le grand chemin que les jeunes gens avaient déblayé', so 'cleared' is his reading (guess). ꜭaholab 'the boys', the twins. cochoch 'their house' (narrative, so k-). ca tocol is written with plain c where Brasseur has togol; he translates 'qui allait tout droit à leur maison', and 'running straight' is taken from him (inferred); the toggle respells the letters, as the tocol of 004.

sentences.t: xa cu yacal ri zamahel xopon ruꜭ catit. Are cut que chahic ta xul canoc vzamahel Xibalba.
sentences.l: just then raised(?) the messenger(s) arrived with their-grandmother. This then they eating(?) when arrived (canoc) its-messenger(s) Xibalba.
sentences.i: and the messengers came straight (?) to the grandmother. They were eating (?) when the messengers of Xibalba arrived.
sentences.n: yacal 'raised, set up' (as 016's yacal ha); here taken with Brasseur's 'directement', 'straight' (inferred). xopon 'arrived' is singular for the messengers, as in earlier parts. ruꜭ catit 'to their grandmother' (narrative, k-). que chahic: the division is unclear. Brasseur prints qu'echahic and translates 'ils étaient occupés à manger'; read as que + echahic 'eating' (echa 'food', the published echahic) with the e written once (inferred), the letters printed as divided. Who 'they' are is not said; the boys are away at the ball court. xul canoc 'arrived there': canoc 'remaining', here 'there' (as earlier parts). vzamahel Xibalba 'the messengers of Xibalba', v- 'its'.

sentences.t: “Quitzih que petic, quecha ri ahauab,” xeꜭha cut ri vzamahel Xibalba.
sentences.l: “Truly they come, say the lords,” they-said then the its-messenger(s) Xibalba.
sentences.i: “Truly they are to come, say the lords,” said the messengers of Xibalba.
sentences.n: Quitzih 'truly' is written with plain t + z here; it is the quiꜩih of earlier parts, and the toggle gives qitzij. que petic 'they are to come': the t looks like an h in the MS (as often in this hand) and is read with Brasseur. quecha ri ahauab 'the lords say', with plain ch, printed as written.

sentences.t: Ta xchoye cu canoc qui quih cumal ri vzamahel Xibalba: “Vvcubix que tzelavachixic,” xuꜭhax canoc Xmucane.
sentences.l: Then was-set(?) then (canoc) their day by-them the its-messenger(s) Xibalba: “In-seven-days they are-awaited(?),” was-told (canoc) Xmucane.
sentences.i: Then the messengers of Xibalba set (?) their day: “In seven days they will be awaited (?),” Xmucane was told.
sentences.n: xchoye is not otherwise known; Brasseur has 'marquèrent le jour', and 'set' follows him (guess); respelled by the letters. qui quih 'their day' is written with plain qu where Brasseur has gih; the toggle gives q'ij, as 016's tiquil quih (an open question there). cumal 'by them'. tzelavachixic is read as a passive in -ix-, 'they will be awaited' after Brasseur ('ils seront attendus'); the stem is not known (guess). xuꜭhax 'was told' (as published). Xmucane, the grandmother, is named here; in the narrative she is otherwise 'the old woman' (atit) or 'their grandmother'.

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala, xque be tacoc, ix zamahel,” xꜭha ri atit. Xe be curi zamahel, xe tzalihic.
sentences.l: “Good bala, they-shall go be-summoned, you messenger(s),” she-said the old-woman. They-went then-the messenger(s), they-returned.
sentences.i: “Very well, they will go when they are summoned, messengers,” said the old woman. And the messengers went, and went back.
sentences.n: Vꜩ bala 'very well' (house). xque be tacoc 'they shall go to be summoned': x- (future) + que 'they' + be 'go' + tacoc, taq 'send for' + -oc (published). In xꜭha ri atit the r of ri looks like a v in the MS, as often in this hand. curi 'then the', cu + ri. xe tzalihic 'they returned', the ꜩalih of earlier parts written here with plain t + z.

sentences.t: Ta xquiz cut vꜭux ri atit: “Naqui xchin vchah qui taquic ri viy? Mavi quitzih ri Xibalba?
sentences.l: Then it-ended then her-heart the old-woman: “What I-shall say(?) their-summoning the my-grandchildren? Not true the Xibalba?
sentences.i: Then the old woman's heart broke: “What am I to say (?) of this summons of my grandsons? Is it not truly Xibalba?
sentences.n: xquiz vꜭux 'her heart ended': k'is 'end', as earlier parts; Brasseur 'le cœur de la vieille se brisa'. Naqui xchin vchah: naqui 'what', xchin 'I shall' (x- + ch- + in 'I'), vchah as in the last part ('say', inferred). Brasseur reads 'À qui commanderai-je d'aller chercher mes petits-fils?', 'whom shall I tell to fetch'; either fits the letters. qui taquic 'their being summoned', taq + -ic. viy 'my grandchildren', v- 'my' + iy. Mavi quitzih ri Xibalba? 'Is it not truly Xibalba?': she knows who is calling.

sentences.t: Xa quehe rulic zamahel oher, ta xe be camoc ri qui cahau,” xꜭha ri catit, ꜫuz choc pa ha vtuquel.
sentences.l: Just thus its-coming messenger(s) of-old, when they-went to-take(?) the their-father(s),” she-said the their-grandmother, sorrowful(?) entering in house alone.
sentences.i: It was just so that the messengers came long ago, when they went to take their fathers,” said their grandmother, and she went into the house alone, grieving (?).
sentences.n: Brasseur runs Mavi quitzih ri Xibalba (end of the last unit) into this sentence as one question ('N'est-ce pas véritablement de la même manière que vinrent autrefois les envoyés'); the established punctuation divides them. rulic 'its coming': r- 'its' + ul 'come' + -ic. oher 'of old' (ojer). qui cahau 'their fathers': Hunhunahpu and Vucub Hunahpu, summoned in 009. camoc is read 'to take', the 'take' verb (k'am) + -oc, after Brasseur (qam-oc, 'pour prendre leurs pères'), as 015 and 016 decided for this verb; 007's camoc 'let him die' is a different word (kamoq). In xꜭha ri catit the r looks like a v in the MS. ꜫuz: the letter is g-shaped, which this hand uses for ꜭ, but Brasseur's g and 015's ꜫuz decided the tresillo. The sense is uncertain: 015 took it as 'delight' after Brasseur's 'plaisir' there, but here Brasseur has 'seule et triste', and 'grieving' follows him (guess). choc 'entering': ch- + oc 'enter'. ha 'house' (ja). vtuquel 'alone'.

sentences.t: Catecut xcah vlo hun vꜭ chu cayac; cate cu xu chap acanoc, ta xu ya cut pu cab; chi malmat ib curi vꜭ xbinic.
sentences.l: Then fell hither one louse at-its cayac(?); then then she-seized-it up, then she-put-it then in-her hand; wriggling(?) itself then-the louse it-walked.
sentences.i: Then a louse dropped from under her clothes (?); she caught it and picked it up, and put it on her hand; and the louse, wriggling (?), walked.
sentences.n: xcah vlo 'fell, came down hither' (xqaj, as earlier parts). vꜭ 'louse' (uk'), with the g-shaped cuatrillo, Brasseur's Uq. chu cayac: cayac is not otherwise known; Brasseur has 'de dessous (son jupon)', and the English follows him (guess). xu chap 'she seized it' (chap 'catch'), acanoc 'up' (as earlier parts). pu cab 'in her hand'. chi malmat ib: the MS has chimalmatib, divided as Brasseur divides it; malmat is the published 'eagerly (inferred)', ib 'self', and Brasseur has 'se remuant' here and 'en se dandinant' in the next paragraph, so 'wriggling' (inferred). xbinic 'it walked'.

sentences.t: “At viy, chavah tah ca nu taco, que be ta a taca ri viy pa hom?” xuꜭhax ri vꜭ.
sentences.l: “You my-grandchild, you-want (tah) I send-you, they(?) go (ta) you summon the my-grandchildren at ball-court?” was-told the louse.
sentences.i: “My grandchild, would you like me to send you, to go and summon my grandsons at the ball court?” the louse was told.
sentences.n: At viy 'you, my grandchild': she speaks to the louse as to a child of the house. Brasseur's note: 'toi neveu (ou petit-fils)', a familiar address. chavah 'you want': ch- + av- 'you', the form of a- 'you' before a vowel (as v- 'I' in vilo), + ah 'want' (Brasseur ch'av'ah, 'aimerais-tu'). ca nu taco 'that I send (you)': nu 'I' + taco 'send' (inferred). que be ta a taca 'that you go to summon': que is unclear before be, and the English leaves it out; a taca 'you summon' (a- 'you' + taca).

sentences.t: Ta xbec taconel: “Mi xul zamahel ruꜭ ivatit; caꜭha: Cat oponic; vvcubix cut que oponic, cacha vzamahel Xibalba, caꜭha ivatit,” caꜭha, xuꜭhax ri vꜭ.
sentences.l: Then went the-messenger: “Just-now came messenger(s) with your-grandmother; she-says: You arrive; in-seven-days then they arrive, say its-messenger(s) Xibalba, says your-grandmother,” she-says, was-told the louse.
sentences.i: So the messenger went (?) with this word: “Messengers have just come to your grandmother; she says: ‘You are to go there; in seven days they are to go there,’ say the messengers of Xibalba, says your grandmother.” So she said; so the louse was told.
sentences.n: taconel 'one sent, messenger': taq 'send' + agent -onel (inferred), the louse. The words that follow are still what the louse is told to carry (the tag xuꜭhax ri vꜭ), so Ta xbec taconel may be the grandmother's 'go, messenger' rather than narrative; Brasseur runs it into the speech (inferred either way). ivatit 'your (pl.) grandmother', i- 'your' + atit. caꜭha 'she says' (ca- ongoing); cacha vzamahel 'the messengers say' with plain ch, printed as written. Cat oponic 'you (one) are to arrive', and que oponic 'they are to arrive': the messengers' words to her, then the boys; Brasseur has '(Il faut) que tu te prépares dans sept jours et qu'ils viennent'. The final caꜭha repeats the frame once more; three levels of speech are printed inside one pair of quotation marks.

sentences.t: Ta xbec; chi malmat cut xbec. Cubul curi ꜭahol pa be, Tamazul vbi, ri xpec.
sentences.l: Then it-went; wriggling(?) then it-went. Seated then-the boy on road, Tamazul his-name, the toad.
sentences.i: So it went; wriggling (?), it went. Now sitting on the road was a boy, Tamazul by name, the toad.
sentences.n: chi malmat 'wriggling (?)', as in the last paragraph (Brasseur 'en se dandinant'). Cubul 'seated', a positional in -ul (kub'ul). ꜭahol 'boy, young man'. Tamazul is the toad's name, from the Nahuatl word for toad, as Brasseur notes ('de tamacolli, crapaud, en langue nahuatl'); kept as a name. xpec 'toad': Brasseur writes Xpek, his k standing for q, and the modern word is xpeq; the toggle gives xpeq.

sentences.t: “Apa cat be vi?” ꜭha cu ri xpec chire vꜭ.
sentences.l: “Where you go (vi)?” says then the toad to-it louse.
sentences.i: “Where are you going?” said the toad to the louse.
sentences.n: Apa … vi 'where': apa 'where' with vi after the verb, as in earlier parts. cat be 'you are going': k- + at 'you' + be. ꜭha 'says', the ꜭha of earlier parts without x- (ch'a), used of the past.

sentences.t: “Ꜭo ba nu ꜩih chi nu pam; quin be cuꜭ ꜭaholab,” xꜭha ri vꜭ chire Tamazul.
sentences.l: “There-is (ba) my word in my belly; I go with-them boys,” it-said the louse to-him Tamazul.
sentences.i: “There is a word I carry in my belly; I am going to the boys,” said the louse to Tamazul.
sentences.n: Ꜭo ba nu ꜩih chi nu pam 'there is my word in my belly': ꜭo 'there is' with the g-shaped cuatrillo (Brasseur qo), ba a particle Brasseur calls one 'd'élégance et de doute'; pam 'belly'. The louse's formula comes back three more times: it carries the message inside itself, as the animals will carry one another. quin be 'I am going': k- + in 'I' + be. cuꜭ ꜭaholab 'to the boys', 'with them, the boys'.

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala, ma ba cat anaic, ca vilo,” xuꜭhax cu vꜭ ta rumal xpec. “Ma chavah ca nu bico? Chavila na pe quin anic va; xcoh opon chanim.”
sentences.l: “Good bala, not (ba) you run(?), I see-it,” was-told then louse (ta) by toad. “Not you-want I swallow-you? You-shall-see (na pe) I run (va); we-shall arrive quickly.”
sentences.i: “Very well; but you hardly run, I see,” the toad told the louse. “Would you like me to swallow you? You will see how I run; we shall get there quickly.”
sentences.n: anaic, anic 'run' (inferred, after Brasseur 'Tu ne cours guère'; compare anim 'quickly' of earlier parts); respelled by the letters. ca vilo 'I see it': v- 'I' + il 'see' + -o. Ma chavah ca nu bico? 'do you want me to swallow you?' (Brasseur 'Veux-tu que je t'avale'): bico is the swallow verb, written with plain c where Brasseur has bigo (his g = ꜫ); the modern verb is b'iq' and the toggle gives b'iq'o, the word being certain. Chavila 'you shall see': ch- + av- 'you' (before a vowel, as in chavah) + il 'see' + -a. na pe and va are particles not otherwise explained. xcoh opon 'we shall arrive': x- + c- + oh 'we'. chanim 'quickly', the published word.

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala,” xꜭha ri vꜭ chirech xpec.
sentences.l: “Good bala,” it-said the louse to-it toad.
sentences.i: “Very well,” said the louse to the toad.
sentences.n: Vꜩ bala 'very well' (house). chirech 'to it', chi + r- + ech, beside chire in the same use.

sentences.t: Catecut ta xrictaxic rumal xpec. Chi bec nah curi xpec ta xbec, chi mavi ca anic.
sentences.l: Then (ta) it-was-taken-in(?) by toad. Going far then-the toad when it-went, (chi) not it runs.
sentences.i: Then it was taken in (?) by the toad. A long way the toad went, but it did not run.
sentences.n: xrictaxic is not otherwise known; read as a passive in -tax- with -ic, 'it was taken in', after Brasseur 'il se laissa avaler par le Crapaud' (guess); respelled by the letters. The stem may instead be the ric 'find, come upon' of chu rico (003), 'it was received (?) by the toad' (guess either way). Chi bec nah 'going far': Brasseur 'le Crapaud marcha longtemps'. chi mavi ca anic 'not running': ca 'ongoing' + anic. The toad offered to run and does not.

sentences.t: Catecut ta xu cul chicut hun nima cumatz, Zaquicaz vbi.
sentences.l: Then (ta) it-met again-then one great snake, Zaquicaz its-name.
sentences.i: Then in its turn it met a great snake, Zaquicaz by name.
sentences.n: xu cul 'it met': x- + v- + cul 'meet', the verb of the published xculutah 'was met'. cumatz 'snake' is written here with plain t + z; it is the cumaꜩ of earlier parts (kumatz). Zaquicaz is the snake's name. It may contain zaqui 'white', and the toggle spells it so (Brasseur Zakicaz, his k = q). The rest of the name is not known, so it is kept untranslated.

sentences.t: “Apa cat be vi, at Tamazul ꜭahol?” xuꜭhax chic ri xpec rumal Zaquicaz.
sentences.l: “Where you go (vi), you Tamazul boy?” was-told again the toad by Zaquicaz.
sentences.i: “Where are you going, Tamazul, my boy?” the toad was asked in turn by Zaquicaz.
sentences.n: The question is the toad's own question to the louse, now put to the toad. at Tamazul ꜭahol 'you, Tamazul, boy': Brasseur 'Tamazul, mon garçon'. xuꜭhax chic 'was told in turn'.

sentences.t: “In zamahel; ꜭo nu ꜩih chi nu pam,” xꜭha chicut xpec chire cumatz.
sentences.l: “I messenger; there-is my word in my belly,” it-said again-then toad to-it snake.
sentences.i: “I am a messenger; there is a word I carry in my belly,” said the toad to the snake.
sentences.n: In zamahel 'I am a messenger': in 'I', with no verb 'to be', as K'iche' sets two nouns side by side. The toad now claims the louse's message as its own, in the louse's words, without ba.

sentences.t: “Ma ba cat anic, ca vilo; in ta on xquin opon chanim,” xꜭha cu cumatz chire xpec. “Cat oho,” xuꜭhaxic.
sentences.l: “Not (ba) you run, I see-it; I (ta) perhaps I-shall arrive quickly,” it-said then snake to-it toad. “You come(?)” it-was-told.
sentences.i: “You hardly run, I see; I, now, shall get there quickly,” said the snake to the toad. “Come here,” it was told.
sentences.n: The snake makes the toad's offer again. in ta on 'I, rather', on a particle of earlier parts ('perhaps'); Brasseur reads the clause as a question ('n'arriverai-je pas plus vite (que toi)?'). xquin opon 'I shall arrive': x- + qu- + in 'I'. Cat oho 'you come here': cat 'you' + oho, not otherwise known, read after Brasseur 'Viens ici donc' (inferred). xuꜭhaxic 'it was told', the published form.

sentences.t: Catecu xbic chic ri xpec rumal Zaquicaz; ta xu cam ri recha cumatz, que bico v xpec vacamic.
sentences.l: Then was-swallowed again the toad by Zaquicaz; then it-took the its-food snake, they swallow-it their toad today.
sentences.i: Then the toad in its turn was swallowed by Zaquicaz; and so the snake took it for its food: snakes swallow toads to this day.
sentences.n: Catecu 'then', the catecut of earlier parts without its final t. xbic 'was swallowed': the swallow verb (Brasseur x-big), plain c written, b'iq' restored by the toggle as in the last paragraph. xu cam ri recha 'it took its food': cam is the 'take' verb (k'am, as 015 and 016), recha 'its food', r- + echa. que bico v xpec 'they swallow their toad (toads)': Brasseur's division, v 'their, its' (the MS runs the letters together). vacamic 'now, today'. The text gives the origin of what snakes eat; Brasseur 'C'est depuis lors que les serpents les prennent pour leur nourriture, et aujourd'hui encore ils engloutissent les crapauds'.

sentences.t: Chan curi cumatz ta xbec; xculutah chi vi cut ri cumatz rumal vac, nima ꜩiquin; xbic chi vi ri cumatz rumal vac.
sentences.l: Quick(?) then-the snake when it-went; was-met in-turn (vi) then the snake by falcon, great bird; was-swallowed in-turn (vi) the snake by falcon.
sentences.i: The snake went quickly (?); and the snake in its turn was met by the falcon, a great bird; and the snake in its turn was swallowed by the falcon.
sentences.n: Chan 'quick (?)': not otherwise known; Brasseur 'Le serpent courait en cheminant'. The same word may be the ꜭhanic 'running' of ¶16, where the toad 'does not run' (inferred). xculutah 'was met' (published). vac is a bird of prey; Brasseur's note says 'Vac, qui est un grand oiseau, dit le texte; ailleurs se trouve écrit voc', so it may be the Voc, Huracan's messenger in 009; and in the next sentence the text calls it xic, 'the hawk'. The English calls it 'the falcon', and its cry vacco in ¶11 is its name. nima ꜩiquin 'a great bird' is the text's own gloss. chi vi 'in turn', as earlier parts.

sentences.t: Catepu xopon ri chuvi hom; ta xu cam recha ri xic, que tio v cumatz pa tac huyub.
sentences.l: Then-also it-arrived the on-top-of ball-court; then it-took its-food the hawk, they eat their snake in (tac) mountains.
sentences.i: Then it came to the ball court, up above. And so the hawk took the snake for its food: hawks eat snakes in the mountains.
sentences.n: Catepu 'then', as catepuch. chuvi hom 'above the ball court'. ri xic 'the hawk': the falcon of the last sentence by another name, as Brasseur's note says ('l'oiseau de proie appelé Xic'); xic is the Xic of the lords' names in 009, there kept as a name. que tio v cumatz: Brasseur's division, v 'their' as in que bico v xpec; tio 'eat (flesh)', the published ti + -o; the t looks like an h in the MS and is read with Brasseur. pa tac huyub 'in the mountains', tac the plural word. Again an origin: Brasseur 'C'est depuis lors que l'Epervier en fait sa nourriture et dévore les serpents dans les montagnes'.

sentences.t: Ta xopon puch ri vac, xꜭhacachob chuvi v ꜩuꜩil hom; que quicot curi Hunahpu, Xbalanque, que chaahic.
sentences.l: Then it-arrived also the falcon, it-alighted(?) on-top-of its cornice(?) ball-court; they rejoice then-the Hunahpu, Xbalanque, they play.
sentences.i: So the falcon came and lit (?) on the wall (?) of the ball court, where Hunahpu and Xbalanque were rejoicing, playing ball.
sentences.n: xꜭhacachob is doubtful, read letter for letter: Brasseur has x-chakachob and 's'abattit', so 'lit, alighted' follows him (guess). v ꜩuꜩil hom 'the ball court's tzutzil': Brasseur 'la corniche du jeu de paume'; 'wall' or 'cornice' is his reading (guess), and the word is not the ꜩuꜩ 'cloud' of 001. que quicot curi Hunahpu, Xbalanque: in curi the u looks like an a in the MS (cari) and Brasseur's u is taken. que chaahic 'they are playing'. The court is where the twins began in ¶1.

sentences.t: Ta xopon cut ri vac, ta xoc curi vac: “Vacco, vacco,” xꜭha v oquibal, “vacco.”
sentences.l: Then it-arrived then the falcon, then cried then-the falcon: “Vacco, vacco,” it-said its-crying, “vacco.”
sentences.i: And when the falcon came, the falcon cried out: “Vacco, vacco,” went its cry, “vacco.”
sentences.n: xoc 'it cried' and v oquibal 'its crying, its cry' (oꜫ + -ibal) are written with plain c; the word is oꜫ 'cry, weep' (Brasseur x-og, r'ogibal; modern oq'), certain here from the bird's call, so the toggle supplies the tresillo, xoq', oq'ib'al, as for the restored b'iq' 'swallow' (015's choc 'cried', where the reading was only inferred, was left chok). They are not the oc 'enter' of ¶6. Vacco is the bird's call, its name in the cry. The text has v oquibal with v 'its' written apart.

sentences.t: “Naqui pa ri choquic? Peta ca vvb,” xeꜭha.
sentences.l: “What (pa) the crying? Let-come our blowgun(s),” they-said.
sentences.i: “What is that crying? Our blowguns, quick!” they said.
sentences.n: Naqui pa 'what is it?' (as earlier parts). In ri the r looks like a v in the MS; choquic 'crying' may be written chogquic, and choquic is read (ch- + oꜫ 'cry' + -ic, written with plain c; mt choq'ik, as xoc in the last unit). Peta 'let it come', pe 'come' + ta; Brasseur 'Vite, nos sarbacanes'. ca vvb 'our blowguns' (vvb 'blowgun', house).

sentences.t: Catepuch xqui vvbah ri vac; qui cu tacal vbac vvb chu bac vvach; chi ꜩelet cut xcah vloc.
sentences.l: Then they-blowgunned the falcon; (qui) then landed its-bone blowgun in its-bone its-face; spinning(?) then it-fell hither.
sentences.i: Then they shot the falcon with their blowguns; the pellet of the blowgun struck it in the eye, and spinning (?), it fell down.
sentences.n: Ximénez indents a paragraph here. xqui vvbah 'they shot it with the blowgun': vvb 'blowgun' made a verb with -ah (as 008). qui cu tacal: qui is not clear here and is left out of the English; tacal 'landed, struck' (published, inferred). vbac vvb 'the bone of the blowgun', the pellet; chu bac vvach 'in its eye' (house: vbac vvach 'the eyes'). chi ꜩelet 'spinning (?)': not otherwise known; Brasseur 'il tourna aussitôt sur lui-même'. xcah vloc 'it came down'.

sentences.t: Quitzih vi cut xbe qui chapa; cate xqui ꜩonoh: “Hupa a petic?” xeꜭha chire vac.
sentences.l: Truly (vi) then they-went their catching-it; then they-asked: “How(?) you come?” they-said to-it falcon.
sentences.i: At once they went to catch it, and then they asked: “Why have you come?” they said to the falcon.
sentences.n: Quitzih vi 'truly, at once' (Brasseur 'Sur le coup'). xbe qui chapa 'they went to catch it': qui chapa, qui- 'they' + chap 'catch' + -a. xqui ꜩonoh 'they asked': the plain ligature, given tz'onoj by the toggle as in 016 (the supplied tz' is an open question there). Hupa 'how, why' (as hupacha 'how'); Brasseur 'Que viens-tu faire ici?'.

sentences.t: “Ꜭo ba nu ꜩih chi nu pam; chi cunah ta na vbac nu vach nabe, catecut xchin biyh,” xꜭha ri vac.
sentences.l: “There-is (ba) my word in my belly; that heal (ta na) its-bone my face first, then I-shall say-it,” it-said the falcon.
sentences.i: “There is a word I carry in my belly; but first heal my eye, and then I will tell it,” said the falcon.
sentences.n: The falcon now carries the louse's formula. chi cunah ta na 'heal (it), please, first': chi optative + cunah 'heal' (as in the healers' part, 006), ta na softening the request. vbac nu vach 'my eye' (house). xchin biyh 'I shall say it'. In xꜭha ri vac the r looks like a v in the MS.

sentences.t: “Vꜩ bala,” xeꜭha cut.
sentences.l: “Good bala,” they-said then.
sentences.i: “Very well,” they said.
sentences.n: Vꜩ bala 'very well' (house).

sentences.t: Cate xquelezah zcaquin rih quic ri chaah, xqui coh chi vvach ri vac; loꜩ quic xu binaah cumal.
sentences.l: Then they-took-out a-little its-surface rubber the ball, they-put-it at its-face the falcon; lotz rubber it-was-named by-them.
sentences.i: Then they took off a little of the rubber of the ball and put it on the falcon's eye; they called it lotz quic.
sentences.n: xquelezah 'they took out': x- + qu- (qui- before a vowel) + elezah 'take out' (the elezan of earlier parts). zcaquin 'a little' (as earlier parts). rih quic ri chaah 'the surface of the rubber of the ball': rih 'back, surface', quic 'rubber' (as earlier parts, the ball being of rubber), chaah 'ball, play'; Brasseur 'un peu de la gomme de la balle avec laquelle ils jouaient'. xqui coh 'they put it' (coh 'put'). loꜩ quic is the name given to the remedy; Brasseur's note calls Lotzquiq 'une herbe américaine des tropiques, appelée par les Mexicains Xocoyolli', and says the people used it to remove cataracts; kept untranslated. xu binaah cumal 'it was named by them': the form has the ergative v- written, as 015's xu binaah, with cumal 'by them'.

sentences.t: Libah chicut xcachoh cumal; vꜩ chic vmucubal ri vac xuxic.
sentences.l: At-once then it-was-cachoh(?) by-them; good again its-seeing the falcon it-became.
sentences.i: At once it was done (?) by them, and the falcon's sight was good again.
sentences.n: Libah chicut 'at once then': libah chi 'at once' (as 016). xcachoh is not otherwise known, and Brasseur does not translate it apart ('et en même temps la vue du Vac se trouva parfaitement guérie par eux'); 'done' is a guess, respelled by the letters. vmucubal 'its seeing, its sight': v- + muc 'look' + -ubal, the means of doing (inferred). xuxic 'it became'.

sentences.t: “Chabiyh cut,” xeꜭha chire vac.
sentences.l: “You-say-it then,” they-said to-it falcon.
sentences.i: “Now tell it,” they said to the falcon.
sentences.n: Chabiyh 'you say it': ch- + a- 'you' + biyh, with plain ch as in 016.

sentences.t: Catecut xu xavah nima cumatz. “Caꜭhau oc,” xeꜭha chic chire cumatz.
sentences.l: Then it-vomited great snake. “Speak (oc),” they-said again to-it snake.
sentences.i: Then it brought up the great snake. “Speak, you,” they said in turn to the snake.
sentences.n: xu xavah 'it vomited it' (xawaj, as earlier parts). Caꜭhau oc 'speak (now)': the MS has caghauoc; ca + ꜭhau 'speak' (the ꜭhauic of earlier parts, with the g-shaped cuatrillo; Brasseur Ca chau-oc) + oc; Brasseur 'Parle donc, toi'.

sentences.t: “Ve,” xꜭha chicut, ta xu xauah chi xpec.
sentences.l: “Yes,” it-said again-then, then it-vomited again toad.
sentences.i: “Yes,” it said, and brought up the toad.
sentences.n: Ve 'yes' (as 014). xu xauah is the same verb as xavah, written here with u for v. chi 'in turn' (chik).

sentences.t: “Naquipa a taquiquil ca ꜩihon oc?” xuchax chicuri xpec. “Ꜭo ba nu ꜩih chi nu pam,” xꜭha chicuri xpec.
sentences.l: “What your errand you speak (oc)?” was-told again-then-the toad. “There-is (ba) my word in my belly,” it-said again-then-the toad.
sentences.i: “What is this errand you have to tell?” the toad was asked. “There is a word I carry in my belly,” said the toad.
sentences.n: taquiquil 'errand, message': taq 'send' + -iquil (inferred; Brasseur takikil, 'le message'). ca ꜩihon oc 'you are telling': ꜩihon 'talk, tell' (as earlier parts). xuchax 'was told' is written with plain ch; printed as written, and the toggle gives xuch'ax as the published xuchax. chicuri 'again then the', chic + cu + ri written as one word. Brasseur prints Nakipa qo takikil, with qo 'there is' where the text has a 'your'; the establishment log does not discuss it, and a is kept as established.

sentences.t: Catecut xu tih, xa bic, mahabi xu xauah; xa quehe chu caxꜩ vchi chu tiho; xma ꜭo vi chu xauah.
sentences.l: Then it-tried, just swallowing(?), nothing it-vomited; just thus caxꜩ(?) its-mouth as-it tried; not there-was (vi) its-vomiting.
sentences.i: Then it tried, it only gulped (?), and brought up nothing; only its mouth slavered (?) as it tried; nothing came of its retching.
sentences.n: xu tih 'it tried', and chu tiho 'as it tried' (the published tih, tiho 'try'; in tiho the t looks like an h in the MS). xa bic 'just swallowing': the swallow verb, as in ¶10 (not the published bic 'going', b'ik); Brasseur has 'comme s'il étouffait'. chu caxꜩ vchi: the MS has chucaꜩ with an x written above the a, printed in place; Brasseur reads chu qaxah u chi and translates 'sa bouche se couvrait comme de bave'. The word and its sense are uncertain, and 'slavered' follows Brasseur (guess). xma ꜭo vi chu xauah 'there was nothing to its vomiting', xma 'not' + ꜭo 'there is'.

sentences.t: Catecut xrah chaiic cumal ꜭaholab: “At ꜭaxtoy,” xuꜭhaxic; ta xiic vvarachac chi acan; xcah cu baquil vvarachac chi acan.
sentences.l: Then it-wanted beating(?) by-them boys: “You deceiver,” it-was-told; then xiic(?) its-rump(?) with foot; came-down then the-bone its-rump(?) to leg.
sentences.i: Then the boys were about to beat it (?): “You cheat,” it was told; and they kicked (?) its rump (?) with a foot; and the bone of its rump (?) came down to its legs.
sentences.n: xrah chaiic 'it wanted the beating', that is, the beating was about to happen: xrah is active, x- + r- 'it' + ah 'want', the fixed construction of earlier parts with no doer of its own, and cumal ꜭaholab names the boys; chaiic is printed as written, read after Brasseur's chayic ('voulaient le maltraiter'; inferred). At ꜭaxtoy 'you deceiver': the g-shaped cuatrillo; Brasseur qaxtok, 'Tu es un imposteur'. It may be the published ꜭaxtoꜭ 'deceiver', here ending in y; respelled by the letters. ta xiic vvarachac chi acan: xiic is clear in the MS, where Brasseur has x-yicu va r'achak, translated 'en lui donnant du pied au derrière'; 'kicked' and 'rump' are his reading (guess). vvarachac (twice) is not otherwise known; Brasseur renders it the second time as 'son échine', 'its spine'. acan 'foot, leg' is printed without a possessor both times (Brasseur chi r'akan the second time); it is the leg word of the published racan (rakan), and the toggle gives akan to match, not the aq'an of acan 'up' (as acanoc in ¶7). baquil 'its bone' (b'aqil). This, it seems, is why the toad's back sits so low.

sentences.t: Xu tih chicut; xa quehe chu chub vchi.
sentences.l: It-tried again-then; just thus spat(?) its-mouth.
sentences.i: It tried again, but only its mouth frothed (?).
sentences.n: chu chub vchi 'its mouth spat': chub 'spit' (inferred; Brasseur 'qu'une sorte de bave autour de sa bouche'). The sentence repeats the frame of chu caxꜩ vchi in the last unit.

sentences.t: Catepuch xqui rech vchi ri xpec; xrech cumal ꜭaholab; xqui zucah pu chi.
sentences.l: Then they-opened(?) its-mouth the toad; it-was-opened(?) by-them boys; they-searched in mouth.
sentences.i: Then they opened (?) the toad's mouth; it was opened (?) by the boys, and they searched inside its mouth.
sentences.n: xqui rech 'they opened (?)' and xrech 'it was opened (?)': the active and the passive of one verb, rech, not otherwise known and not the rech 'of him' of earlier parts; Brasseur 'ils ouvrirent la bouche au Crapaud' (guess). vchi 'its mouth'. xqui zucah 'they searched': written with plain z where Brasseur has tzukuh, the ꜩucuh 'seek' of 007; respelled by the letters (sukaj). pu chi 'in its mouth', pu 'in'.

sentences.t: Xa cu nacal ri vꜭ chava re xpec, xa pu chi ꜭo vi; mana xu bico, xa quehe xa bic.
sentences.l: Just then stuck(?) the louse at-edge(?) teeth(?) toad, just in mouth it-was (vi); not it-swallowed-it, just thus just swallowed.
sentences.i: The louse was just stuck (?) in the toad's gums (?); it was only in its mouth. The toad had not swallowed it; it only seemed swallowed.
sentences.n: nacal 'stuck (?)': not otherwise known; Brasseur 'se trouvait arrêté'. chava re xpec: the MS has chavare and Brasseur chuva re; the English follows his 'dans les gencives du Crapaud' (guess), as if chava were 'at the edge of' and re 'teeth'. Respelled by the letters. mana xu bico 'it did not swallow it'; xa quehe xa bic 'it was just as if swallowed' (Brasseur 'mais seulement comme s'il l'avait avalé'). So the toad, which offered in ¶8 to carry the louse by swallowing it, never had it inside: the toad is the one fooled (xchacatah in the next unit; Brasseur 'fut joué').

sentences.t: Quehe cut xchacatah vi ri xpec; mavi calah vvach recha xqui yao; ruꜭ mavi ꜭhanic; xa v chac cumatz xuxic.
sentences.l: Thus then was-defeated (vi) the toad; not clear its-face its-food they-give-it; and not it-runs(?); just its-work(?) snake it-became.
sentences.i: So the toad was beaten: no one knows what kind of food is given it; it cannot run (?); it became mere prey (?) for the snakes.
sentences.n: xchacatah 'was defeated, brought down' (published); Brasseur has 'C'est ainsi que fut joué le Crapaud'. mavi calah vvach recha xqui yao 'what its food is like is not clear, which they give it': calah 'clear' (q'alaj, restored as earlier parts), vvach 'its face, its kind'. ruꜭ 'and, with it'. ꜭhanic: the g-shaped cuatrillo (Brasseur ch'anic), read 'run' after Brasseur 'il ne sait pas non plus courir' (inferred); compare Chan in ¶10. xa v chac cumatz: the image has v chac clearly, where Brasseur prints xa u bi cumatz ('est fait de la chair des serpents'); chac is taken as 'work', as 006's vchac 'its work', and 'prey' is a guess. The passage ends the origin stories: snakes eat toads.

sentences.t: “Caꜩihon oc,” xuꜭhax chicut ri vꜭ; ta xu biyh cu vꜩih: “Caꜭha ri ivatit, ix ꜭaholab: He a taca;
sentences.l: “You-speak (oc),” was-told again-then the louse; then it-said then its-word: “She-says the your-grandmother, you boys: Go(?) you summon;
sentences.i: “Speak now,” the louse was told; and it gave its message: “Your grandmother says, boys: ‘Go and summon them;
sentences.n: Caꜩihon oc 'speak now', ca + ꜩihon 'talk' + oc, as ca ꜩihon oc in ¶14. vꜩih 'its word, its message'. The message keeps the grandmother's own words to the louse: He a taca 'go, summon (them)', he 'go' (inferred, as in ¶2) + a taca 'you summon' (Brasseur 'Va les appeler'). The levels of speech are printed inside one pair of quotation marks; the English marks the inner level with single quotes.

sentences.t: xul tacol que ca pe chi Xibalba, vzamahel Hun Came, Vvcub Came: Vvcubix que vlic varal, coh chaah vi;
sentences.l: came summoner(s) they come from Xibalba, its-messenger(s) Hun Came, Vvcub Came: In-seven-days they come here, we play (vi);
sentences.i: summoners have come, who come from Xibalba, the messengers of Huncame and Vucub Came: In seven days let them come here, we will play;
sentences.n: xul tacol 'summoners have come': xul 'came'; in the MS the u looks like an a (xal) and Brasseur's u is taken. tacol 'summoner, one who sends for' (published, taq + -ol). que ca pe chi Xibalba 'who come from Xibalba': que 'they', ca 'ongoing', chi 'from'. Hun Came is written as two words, the published Huncame. que vlic 'they come here', vl 'arrive here' + -ic. The lords' words, as in ¶3.

sentences.t: chi pe ri quetzabal, quic, bate, pachcab, quum; are chi caztah vvach varal, queꜭha ahauab.
sentences.l: let-come the their-gear, rubber, ring(s), hand-guard(s), leather; this that revive its-face here, say lords.
sentences.i: let their gear come with them, the rubber ball, the rings, the hand-guards, the leather, so that their faces may come alive (?) here, say the lords.
sentences.n: chi pe 'let it come'. quetzabal 'their gear for play': qu- 'their' + etz 'play' + -abal; written here with plain t + z, it is the queꜩabal of 016, and the toggle gives that part's ketz'ab'al (etzanem and etzanic in ¶2–3 likewise take etz'). The gear as in 009/010 and 016: quic 'the rubber (ball)', bate 'rings', pachcab 'hand-guards' (Brasseur pachgab), quum 'leather' (Brasseur tzuum; 'cuirasses'). chi caztah vvach 'that its face revive': the MS has catzatz or caztahz, read caztah after Brasseur's qaztah; caztah is the published 'revive' (k'astaj), and Brasseur translates 'qu'ici se vivifie leur visage'. The sense, perhaps 'that they may enjoy themselves here', is uncertain.

sentences.t: Xul quitzih, cacha ri ivatit. Ta xi petic. Quitzih caꜭha ri ivatit; coquic, ca ziquinic ivatit; xi petic.”
sentences.l: They-came truly, says the your-grandmother. Then I came. Truly says the your-grandmother; she-weeps, she calls-out your-grandmother; I came.”
sentences.i: They have truly come, says your grandmother.’ So I came. Truly your grandmother says so; your grandmother is weeping and calling out; so I came.”
sentences.n: cacha ri ivatit 'says your grandmother', with plain ch, printed as written. xi petic 'I came': Brasseur's note says the i after x- stands for in 'I', the n dropped ('le n étant retranché par euphonie'); in the second xi petic the t looks like an h in the MS. coquic 'she weeps': written with plain c (Brasseur c'ogic), c- + oꜫ 'cry, weep' + -ic, and the toggle supplies the tresillo, koq'ik, as for xoc in ¶11. ca ziquinic 'she calls out' (as earlier parts; Brasseur 'elle se lamente'). The grandmother's message ends here.

sentences.t: “Ma quitzih?” xeꜭha cut ꜭaholab chi qui ꜭux, ta xqui tao.
sentences.l: “Not true?” they-said then boys in their heart, when they-heard-it.
sentences.i: “Can it be true?” the boys said in their hearts when they heard it.
sentences.n: Ma quitzih? 'is it not true?', 'can it be true?' (Brasseur 'Serait-ce bien vrai'). chi qui ꜭux 'in their hearts', to themselves. xqui tao 'they heard it', ta 'hear' + -o.

sentences.t: Huzu xe petic; xe opon cut ruꜭ catit; xa e pixabai chire catit xebec.
sentences.l: At-once they-came; they-arrived then with their-grandmother; just they taking-leave to-her their-grandmother they-went.
sentences.i: At once they came, and reached their grandmother; they went only to take their leave of their grandmother.
sentences.n: Huzu 'at once' (jusuk, as earlier parts). xe petic: the t looks like an h in the MS. catit 'their grandmother', narrative (k-). pixabai 'taking leave': pixab 'counsel, charge' (earlier parts) + -ai; Brasseur 'uniquement pour prendre congé de leur aïeule'. e 'they (are)'.

sentences.t: “Hona, ix catit; xa oh pixabay ive.
sentences.l: “We-go (na), you our-grandmother; just we taking-leave to-you.
sentences.i: “We are going, grandmother; we have come only to take our leave of you.
sentences.n: Ximénez indents a paragraph here. Hona 'we go': ho, the form of 'go' with oh 'we' (as 010), + na; Brasseur 'Nous partons'. ix catit 'you, our grandmother', the twins speaking (q-). pixabay is the pixabai of the last unit spelled with y. ive 'to you (pl.)'. They speak to the grandmother and their mother together.

sentences.t: Vae cute retal ca ꜩih xchi ca canah: huhun xchi ca tic chire va ah; chu nicahal cochoch xchi ca tic vi.
sentences.l: This then-indeed its-sign our word we-shall leave: each we-shall plant at-it this cane; at-its middle our-house we-shall plant (vi).
sentences.i: Here is the sign of our word that we shall leave: each of us will plant a cane here; in the middle of our house we will plant it.
sentences.n: Vae cute 'here, then': vae 'this', cute 'then', as earlier parts. retal 'its sign': r- + etal 'sign' (house vetal). xchi ca canah 'we shall leave it', ca 'we'. huhun 'each, one each'. xchi ca tic 'we shall plant': tic 'plant'; in both places the t looks like an h in the MS (cahic) and is read with Brasseur. va ah 'this cane': ah 'cane, reed' (Brasseur 'une canne'), not the ah 'one of' of names. chu nicahal cochoch 'in the middle of our house': nicahal, nicah 'middle' + -al; cochoch is 'our house' (q-) in the twins' mouth.

sentences.t: Are retal ca camic, ve chi chaquihic: Mi pa xe camic, quixꜭha, ta chi chaquihic.
sentences.l: This its-sign our death, if it dries: Already (pa) they-died? you-shall-say, when it dries.
sentences.i: It is the sign of our death, if it dries up: ‘Have they died?’ you will say, if it dries.
sentences.n: ca camic 'our death'. ve 'if'. chi chaquihic 'it dries': chi + chaquih 'dry' (the published chaqi'j, restored) + -ic; written with plain c. Mi pa xe camic? 'have they died?', mi pa the question of earlier parts. quixꜭha 'you (pl.) shall say'. The couplet runs on into the next unit: death if the cane dries, life if it sprouts.

sentences.t: Ve cut ta chi pe vtux: E pa cazlic, quixꜭha cut.
sentences.l: If then (ta) it comes its-sprout: They (pa) alive? you-shall-say then.
sentences.i: But if it puts out a shoot: ‘Are they alive?’ you will say.
sentences.n: chi pe vtux 'its shoot comes': vtux 'its sprout, its flower' (inferred; Brasseur 'Mais si elle vient à fleurir'); respelled by the letters. E pa cazlic 'are they alive?': e 'they' + pa (as mi pa) + cazlic 'living', written with plain c where Brasseur has qazlic (his q = ꜭ); it is the word of ꜭazlem 'life', the word certain, and the toggle gives k'aslik. Brasseur reads this one as a statement ('Ils sont vivants'); the English keeps both halves as questions, as the text pairs them.

sentences.t: Ix catit, ix pu ca chuch, mix oquic; ꜭo retal ca ꜩih ca canahic ivuꜭ,” xeꜭha.
sentences.l: You our-grandmother, you also our mother, not-you weep; there-is its-sign our word remaining with-you,” they-said.
sentences.i: Grandmother, and you, our mother, do not weep: here is the sign of our word that stays with you,” they said.
sentences.n: ix pu ca chuch 'and you, our mother': pu is in the MS but not in Brasseur. mix oquic 'do not weep': mi 'not' + ix 'you (pl.)' (as 014) + oquic, oꜫ 'weep' + -ic with plain c (Brasseur m'yx ogic), mt oq'ik as xoc in ¶11; not the oquic 'entering' (okik) of earlier parts. ꜭo retal 'there is the sign', with the g-shaped cuatrillo (Brasseur qo). ca canahic 'remaining', ca 'ongoing' + canah 'stay' + -ic. ivuꜭ 'with you (pl.)', i- + uꜭ 'company', as ruꜭ, cuꜭ. Brasseur's note: 'il y a ce signe de notre parole qui est resté avec vous'.

sentences.t: Ta xebec; hun xu tic Hunahpu, hun chicu xticou Xbalanque;
sentences.l: Then they-went; one he-planted Hunahpu, one again-then planted(?) Xbalanque;
sentences.i: Then they went: one was planted by Hunahpu, and the other by Xbalanque;
sentences.n: The manuscript has hun nahpu, a misprint for Hunahpu, corrected here: the n is written twice across the word space. In xu tic the u looks like an a in the MS (xa), and Brasseur's u is taken; xu tic 'he planted it', v- 'he' + tic. xticou: the MS has xti at the end of one line and cou at the start of the next, and Brasseur prints x-ucou; read here as the same tic 'plant' with -ou, the agent-focus form of 014's xe chacouic, 'it was Xbalanque who planted it' (inferred; in 015 the doer of such a form stands before the verb, here it follows). chicu 'again then', the other one.

sentences.t: xa pa ha xu tic vi; mana pa huyub tah, mana ipu pa rax vleu tah, xa pa chaquih vleu chu nicahal vpa cochoch xqui tic vi canoc.
sentences.l: just in house he-planted (vi); not in mountain (tah), not also in green earth (tah), just in dry earth at-its middle its-inside their-house they-planted (vi) (canoc).
sentences.i: they planted them in the house: not in the mountains, nor in green earth, but in dry earth, in the middle of the inside of their house, they planted them and left them there.
sentences.n: xa pa ha 'just in the house': ha 'house' (ja). xu tic vi is singular ('he planted'), where the sentence ends with the plural xqui tic for the same act; the English gives 'they' for both. mana … tah 'not …', twice, with ipu 'nor (also)', i + pu (Brasseur mana-Ipu). rax vleu 'green earth', moist ground (Brasseur 'une terre humide'), set against chaquih vleu 'dry earth'. vpa cochoch 'the inside of their house', v- 'its' + pa 'inside'. xqui tic vi canoc 'they planted them there, to stay'. The canes are planted where they cannot live by the soil, so that only the twins' life can keep them green (inferred from the sign just given).
